string-array.name: language_fact_bodies
string-array.item: English has borrowed words from more than 350 different languages, making its vocabulary one of the most \"global\" and hybrid among all modern languages.
Papua New Guinea has more than 800 living languages — roughly 12% of all languages in the world spoken in a single country.
The Khmer alphabet contains 74 letters and is considered the longest alphabet among writing systems still in active use.
Every two weeks a language dies in the world — when its last speaker passes away, an entire cultural memory disappears with them.
Esperanto is the most widely spoken constructed language. About 2 million people use it, and thousands consider it their native tongue.
The Chinese Kangxi dictionary contains over 47,000 characters, but knowing about 3,000 is enough to read a newspaper fluently.
Basque is not related to any known European language — its origin remains a mystery to linguists.
Finnish has no grammatical gender: a single pronoun \"hän\" means both \"he\" and \"she\".
Vietnamese has six tones: the same word pronounced with different intonations can have up to six different meanings.
The longest German word — \"Donaudampfschiffahrtselektrizitätenhauptbetriebswerkbauunterbeamtengesellschaft\" — is 79 letters long.
Latin is considered \"dead\", yet it remains the official language of the Vatican and is still used in science, medicine, and law.
About half of the world\'s 7,000 living languages have no writing system — they exist only in oral tradition.
